description:
Figure: Model overview of the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture.
- Shows the process of transforming an image into a sequence of vectors for classification.
- Steps include splitting the image into fixed-size patches, linearly embedding each patch, adding position embeddings, and feeding the sequence to a standard Transformer encoder.
- Includes an extra learnable "classification token" for classification.
- Inspired by Vaswani et al. (2017).

caption: Figure 2: Breakdown of VTAB performance in Natural , Specialized , and Structured task groups.
description:
## Figure Description
The figure is a bar chart comparing the accuracy of different models across various task groups. The models include ViT-H/14, BiT-L (R152x4), VIVI-Ex-100% (R50x3), and S4L (R50x1). The task groups are VTAB (19 tasks), Natural (7 tasks), Specialized (4 tasks), and Structured (8 tasks). ViT-H/14 has the highest accuracy across all task groups, followed by BiT-L (R152x4), VIVI-Ex-100% (R50x3), and S4L (R50x1). The accuracy ranges from 65% to 80% across different models and tasks.

caption: Figure 3: Transfer to ImageNet. While large ViT models perform worse than BiT ResNets (shaded area) when pre-trained on small datasets, they shine when pre-trained on larger datasets. Similarly, larger ViT variants overtake smaller ones as the dataset grows.
description:
## Description 1

This graph compares the ImageNet Top 1 Accuracy of various Vision Transformer (ViT) models and BiT ResNets when pre-trained on different datasets. The datasets include ImageNet, ImageNet-21k, and JFT-300M. The ViT models are categorized by size: ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/32, ViT-L/16, and ViT-H/14. The highest accuracy is observed in the ViT-H/14 model pre-trained on JFT-300M, reaching approximately 90%. The lowest accuracy is seen in the ViT-B/16 model pre-trained on ImageNet, around 75%.

## Description 2

The figure displays a line graph showing the ImageNet Top 1 Accuracy of various Vision Transformer (ViT) models and BiT ResNets across three pre-training datasets: ImageNet, ImageNet-21k, and JFT-300M. ViT models include ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/32, ViT-L/16, and ViT-H/14. The highest accuracy is achieved by ViT-H/14 on JFT-300M, around 90%. The lowest accuracy is for ViT-B/16 on ImageNet, approximately 75%.

description:
This figure is a line graph showing the performance of various models in terms of Linear 5-shot ImageNet Top1 accuracy. The x-axis represents the number of JFT pre-training samples, ranging from 10 million to 300 million. The y-axis represents the Linear 5-shot ImageNet Top1 accuracy, ranging from 30% to 70%. The graph includes six series: ViT-L/16, ViT-L/32, ViT-B/32, ViT-b/32, ResNet50x1 (BiT), and ResNet152x2 (BiT). The ViT-L/16 series starts at around 40% and increases to about 70%, while the ViT-L/32 series starts at around 50% and also increases to about 70%. The ViT-B/32 series starts at around 40% and increases to about 60%. The ViT-b/32 series starts at around 40% and increases to about 50%. The ResNet50x1 (BiT) series starts at around 50% and increases to about 60%. The ResNet152x2 (BiT) series starts at around 50% and increases to about 60%.

caption: Figure 13: Performance of Axial-Attention based models, in terms of top-1 accuracy on ImageNet 5-shot linear, versus their speed in terms of number of FLOPs ( left ) and inference time ( left ).
description:
This figure is a scatter plot comparing the performance of various models in terms of ImageNet 5-shot linear top-1 accuracy against their computational cost in exaFLOPs. The highest performing model, AxialViT-B/16, is located at the top right corner with an accuracy of approximately 0.650 and a computational cost of 10^2 exaFLOPs. The lowest performing model, ResNet50, is at the bottom left with an accuracy of around 0.500 and a computational cost of 10^0 exaFLOPs.

Other models include AxialViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-B/32, and AxialResNet50, each positioned between these two extremes. AxialViT-B/32 has an accuracy of about 0.575 and a computational cost of 10^1 exaFLOPs, while ViT-B/16 and ViT-B/32 have accuracies of around 0.550 and computational costs of 10^0 exaFLOPs. AxialResNet50 has an accuracy of approximately 0.525 and a computational cost of 10^0 exaFLOPs.

The main point of this figure is to illustrate the trade-off between the performance and computational cost of various models in image recognition tasks. The scatter plot shows that as the computational cost increases, the ImageNet 5-shot linear top-1 accuracy also increases, indicating that more powerful models (in terms of computational resources) generally achieve higher accuracy. This relationship is evident across different model architectures, including AxialViT, ViT, and ResNet.
